chunks: And you will never be able to be equal [in feeling] between wives, even if you should strive [to do so]; so do not incline completely [toward one] and leave another hanging. And if you amend [your affairs] and fear Allah - then indeed, Allah was ever Forgiving and Merciful.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about treating multiple wives equally?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse distinguishes between 'equal distribution' (qist) in material matters, which is obligatory, and 'emotional equality' (muwaddah), which is subjective and largely beyond human control. The metaphor of the 'suspended wife' (al-mu'allaqa) is interpreted by scholars like Al-Tabarsi as a state of uncertainty and neglect, urging men to avoid extreme partiality that leaves one wife in limbo. This guidance underscores that while perfect justice is unattainable, striving for fairness coupled with God-consciousness (taqwa) remains the spiritual ideal.
